text:
maria: fyi — I'm seeing a small but consistent spike in fncall/structured validation rejects on the canary route (route_id=svc-chat-canary). started ~09:12 UTC, ~0.8% -> now ~4.7%
aj: ouch. any pattern in the payloads?
sarah: pinging logs, grabbing a few samples. looks like the model sometimes returns an array for `tool_response` instead of an object; validator is strict and rejects.
maria: exact validator message: `TypeError: expected object for tool_response, received array`
kevin: can you paste a sample?
sarah: here are two minimal samples (sanitized):
```json
{"request_id":"r-8142","tool_response": []}
{"request_id":"r-8149","tool_response": ["result1","result2"]}
```
maria: thanks. the canary policy routes to a newer tool-adapter that changed how it marshals single vs multiple outputs. not a model change.
aj: what's the current telemetry sampling for rejected fncalls? IIRC we only sample 0.1% globally which undercounts this.
kevin: yes, console shows ~0.1% sampling tag for `validation.rejects`. per-route sampling isn't enabled for canaries right now.
maria: proposal: bump sampling to 5% for svc-chat-canary for the next 2 hours, tag samples with `handshake_mismatch=true` and include `route_id` + `model_variant`.
sarah: +1. need the sample payloads surfaced in the console as clickable links, not just counts. ops folks keep asking for trace links.
aj: operationally we have two levers: 1) change validator to coerce arrays->object (lenient) 2) fail-fast and roll the canary back (strict). We should pick based on risk.
kevin: my take: coerce-only for a short window and mark these as `soft_reject` in metrics so we can quantify user-facing impact. If we see semantic losses in outputs, roll back.
maria: concern: coercion could hide adapter bugs and allow broken shapes downstream. Also billing/quotas attribution differs if we soft-accept.
aj: true. also quota accounting: currently rejected fncalls aren't billed, if we soft-accept they will be billed and could surprise finance. Need product ok.
sarah: can we do a hybrid: accept but tag `accepted_via_coercion=true` and ensure cost attribution uses the original route_id with a `coercion` flag? We can then set an internal billing report to exclude those until product signs off.
kevin: that's doable. small infra change to add a `coercion` dimension in metering events.
maria: immediate steps I suggest:
- increase sampling to 5% for svc-chat-canary (maria)
- add telemetry tag `handshake_mismatch` and `coercion_candidate` (sarah)
- deploy a short-lived lenient validator behind a feature flag that converts arrays->[object] for single-element arrays only (aj will own PR)
- gate billing on product approval; for now mark events so finance can filter (kevin)
- if soft-accept rate > 10% of canary traffic or quality regression metrics spike, rollback the canary (deploy-bot will alert)

maria: aj — can you do the PR for lenient validator + flag? we want it behind `fncall_coerce_canary_1809`.
aj: yeah I'll open PR in ~30m. will include unit tests and a quick e2e with the canary route.
sarah: I'll wire the sampling change and make samples link to traces; need a tiny dashboard tile showing `validation.reject_rate` vs `coerced.accept_rate` per route.
kevin: I'll add the metering flag and coordinate with finance to ensure no surprise charges. also will add a billing report filter (tag = `coercion_candidate`).
deploy-bot: [alert] canary svc-chat-canary at 5% currently. monitoring hook configured: validation.reject_rate > 2% for 10m -> page oncall.
maria: deploy-bot thanks — can we add a temporary monitor that pages only if post-coercion-rejects > 2%? i.e. don't page on samples we intend to accept.
aj: ok I can adjust alert rules in the canary stack.
sarah: quick note: console UX — the current rollout timeline UI doesn't clearly show per-variant sampling or the telemetry tags. I'll file a UX ticket to add an expandable per-canary row for telemetry knobs.
maria: make that ticket internal: UX-2140. not blocking the infra work but good to have.
kevin: timeline: infra + sampling in next 1 hour, PR review + merge ~2 hours, behind feature flag for the next 4 hours, then reassess.
aj: I'll annotate the PR with a rollback plan and a migration for metering schema.
sarah: I'll link samples to PR so reviewers can see real failing payloads.
maria: thanks team. If anything spikes to >10% before we finish, we will pause canary. Otherwise we'll proceed with soft-accept and track.
kevin: noted. tagging slack thread with `handshake-mismatch` and `canary-1809`.
aj: PR -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/validator/pulls/492 (draft).
sarah: opened dashboard tile draft: https://console.internal/d/telemetry/validation-canary-1809 (private link).
maria: closing loop — I'll post an update in ~3h with numbers. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks. I'll message finance to expect the `coercion_candidate` flag for a short window.
deploy-bot: [info] scheduled monitor update applied.
maria: done for now. we can pivot if samples show real data corruption.
